methods.label: Combine the arcs into a semicircle
methods.explanation:
Group the two smaller-circle arcs together before adding the path lengths.

[Figure 1](figures/2008_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

A half-turn about the common center carries the lower-left smaller-circle arc onto the upper-right smaller-circle arc, so these arcs have equal lengths. Let each have length \(s\).

The upper-right outer-circle arc from \(A\) to \(K\) covers the same fraction of its circle as the upper-right inner arc. The outer radius is twice the inner radius, so its circumference, and therefore this corresponding arc, is twice as long. Its length is \(2s\), exactly the combined length of the two inner arcs.

Thus the total curved distance equals the traveled upper-left outer arc plus the upper-right outer arc. Together they form the upper semicircle of radius \(20\), with length
\[
\frac12(2\pi\cdot20)=20\pi.
\]
The straight portions are two radial gaps between the circles and one diameter of the smaller circle. Their total length is
\[
(20-10)+2\cdot10+(20-10)=40.
\]
The aardvark runs \(\boxed{20\pi+40}\) meters, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
